title: 21. Composition, inheritance, abstract base class, what?

examples.explanation: Convert table cells into the supplied typed record.

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod from collections import namedtuple from dataclasses import dataclass, field import os from pathlib import Path from typing import List, NamedTuple, Optional, Union TMP = Path(os.getenv("TMP", "/tmp")) import html as _html import re as _re class Soup: """Stand-in for BeautifulSoup (the judge has no third-party packages). Soup(html).find_all("table") returns the tables as Table objects. str(table) is the table's HTML. table.rows() returns the text of each cell (th or td), row by row. """ def __init__(self, markup: str): self.markup = markup def find_all(self, name: str) -> list: if name != "table": raise NotImplementedError("this Soup only finds tables") return [Table(m.group(0)) for m in _re.finditer(r"", self.markup, _re.S | _re.I)] class Table(str): def rows(self) -> list: rows = [] for row in _re.findall(r"", self, _re.S | _re.I): cells = _re.findall(r"]*>(.*?)", row, _re.S | _re.I) rows.append([" ".join(_html.unescape(_re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", c)).split()) for c in cells]) return rows # Add type hints: turn these into typing.NamedTuple classes. # Candidate: name (str), votes (str) # LeaderBoard: Candidate (str), Average (str), Delegates (int), # Contributions (str), Coverage (int) # Poll: Poll (str), Date (str), Sample (int), Sanders (float), # Biden (float), Gabbard (float), Spread (str) Candidate = namedtuple("Candidate", "name votes") LeaderBoard = namedtuple("LeaderBoard", "Candidate Average Delegates Contributions Coverage") Poll = namedtuple("Poll", "Poll Date Sample Sanders Biden Gabbard Spread") @dataclass class File: """File represents a filesystem path. Variables: name: str -- The filename that will be created on the filesystem. path: Path -- Path object created from TMP and the name passed in. Methods: [property] data: -> Optional[str] -- If the file exists, it returns its contents. If it does not exist, it returns None. """ name: str @dataclass class Web: """Web object. Variables: url: str -- The URL of the site. file: File -- File object where the HTML of the site is cached. Methods: [property] data: -> Optional[str] -- The contents of the cached file, or None. (The original downloads the page when the file is missing; the judge is offline, so return the file data.) [property] soup: -> Soup -- A Soup object of the HTML data. """ url: str file: File class Site(ABC): """Site abstract base class. Its constructor receives web: Web. Methods: find_table(loc: int = 0) -> str -- The HTML of the table at index loc in the page (str() of the Soup table). Not abstract. [abstract] parse_rows(table: str) -> Union[List[LeaderBoard], List[Poll]] -- Turn the data rows (skip the header row) into namedtuples. [abstract] polls(table: int = 0) -> Union[List[LeaderBoard], List[Poll]] -- parse_rows of find_table(table). [abstract] stats(loc: int = 0) -- Print the statistics. def test_find_table(rcp):
    first, third = rcp.find_table(0), rcp.find_table(2)
    assert isinstance(third, str)
    assert first.startswith("<table") and 'id="t1"' in first
    assert 'id="t3"' in third and "Emerson" in third
    assert "Emerson" not in first

test_nyt_polls.title: test_nyt_polls
test_nyt_polls.code:
def test_nyt_polls(nyt):
    polls = nyt.polls()
    assert len(polls) == 4
    assert polls[0] == LeaderBoard("Pete Buttigieg", "10%", 25, "$76.2m", 3)
    assert polls[2] == LeaderBoard("Joseph R. Biden Jr.", "26%", 15, "$60.6m", 1)
    assert all(isinstance(p, LeaderBoard) for p in polls)
    assert nyt.parse_rows(nyt.find_table(0)) == polls

courseHelp.title: Course help
courseHelp.body:
Write your implementation above the supplied tests. Run checks the sample tests. Submit checks all supplied tests. Keep the tests and runner unchanged.

For an older saved solution, use **+** beside the editor tabs to open the current template. Copy your implementation into the new tab. Your old tab stays in place.

The template and tests are recreations based on the public bite description. This is an offline version. The judge has no network and no BeautifulSoup, so the template supplies a small `Soup` class with `find_all("table")`, and `Web.data` reads the cached HTML file (the tests create it). The sample pages in the tests are fictional and contain only the tables that are used. Everything else follows the description: the typed namedtuples, `File`, `Web`, the `Site` abstract base class, the two parsers, and the exact output formats. Python 3.11. Use the standard library. No network access.

[Original Pybites exercise](https://pybitesplatform.com/bites/composition-inheritance-abstract-base-class-what/)
